checks: Relative interior of the prescribed point bounds coefficient norms through its centered inball. A limit boundary chart is nonnegative and its zero is attained on a sampled fiber because the chart is affine on the convex hull of the samples.

At r>=d the accepted divergence rules out an escaping bounded sublevel, including a zero chart restriction on an entire fiber. Distinct relative charts differ on positive sampled volume, so strict scalar convexity gives strict functional convexity.

Uniform positivity near the minimizer permits differentiation; the resulting stationary identity is exactly the escort mean equation. The unique multiplicative factor fixes the inverse-power mean, and any parameter with that escort mean yields the same stationary chart.

Direct substitution verifies the interval integrals, including y=1/2 by the constant case. Independent rational evaluations on both signs of the slope give normalized inverse square one and the desired inverse-cube mean.

dependencies.hypotheses: A limiting positive affine sequence on a fixed positive d-fiber with a nonnegative boundary limit vanishing somewhere is the stated divergence case for r>=d.

overlap.comparison: Supplies the endpoint blow-up used for compactness; it does not give the existence or uniqueness of the escort chart for a prescribed full-space relative-interior mean.
Treats minimizing a different buffered objective over positive charts, not the escort-mean parametrization.

readability: The statement, sign conventions and scope are explicit.
review_method: Independent cold proof read followed by source, predecessor and exact arithmetic checks
summary: Strict convex minimization of normalized inverse power over the positive affine charts gives existence and uniqueness, with an exact interval example.
